label: Category Card
title: Category Card
summary: Use a Category Card for one category in a horizontal rail: a picture, a one- or two-word label, and an optional badge.
corePrinciple: One picture, one word, one tap.

anatomy.title: A badge, a picture, and a label
anatomy.description: A 60 px white tile stacks a square picture over a one-line label, with an optional badge on its top edge. Here a Coin Icon Capsule in imageSlot stands in for your category art.
blocks: Optional: badge sets one short word, cut off past 38 px.
imageSource fills a 36 px square; imageSlot takes any node instead, as here.

configuration.title: Badge and brand colour
configuration.description: badge adds a short tag on the card’s top edge; leave it out for none. AppearanceBrand colours the badge, Tertiary blue by default, and anything in imageSlot gets the same modes, so the Icon Capsule follows it. Emphasis Medium or Low makes the badge pale. Radius rounds the corners of the default image only. The card’s surface, border, and label look the same in every mode.

states.title: Idle, active, and disabled
states.description: active turns the border gold on the category that’s showing. The card keeps no state of its own: the screen sets active on one card and moves it in onPress. A pressed card dims to 85 %; disabled dims it to half and stops onPress.

sizing.title: 60 px wide, as tall as its content
sizing.description: The card is 60 px wide unless you set width, and as tall as its content: 4 px padding, the picture, a 6 px gap, and a 16 px label line. With the default 36 px image it’s 68 px tall; the 42 px capsule here makes it 74. A badge sits 11 px above the card, and every card keeps that room in its layout, with or without a badge.

content.title: One or two short words
content.description: Name the category in a word or two, and keep the badge to one short word that doesn’t repeat it. A label wider than the card spills past both edges by default. singleLine={false} wraps it onto two lines and makes that card taller; add disableTruncation={false} as well for one line that ends in an ellipsis, as Figma shows.

inContext.title: A category rail on the Invest screen
inContext.description: The screen keeps the selected category and sets active on that card; each card’s onPress selects it. Every card keeps 11 px above it for a badge, so cards with and without one line up in the rail.

sources.title: Use the public Category Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78, built from Biscuit’s main at c7d3348 (19 October) and taken from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Category Card has a State variant (Idle, Active) and a badge on or off; in code, active and the badge text are props. Without an image the card shows a plain light square, so these examples put a Coin Icon Capsule in imageSlot. The label’s font token is spelt “Jio Type Var”, so the label shows in a fallback serif font until the token is fixed. Figma ends a long label in an ellipsis; the package lets it spill unless you change singleLine and disableTruncation. Every card keeps 11 px above it for a badge, so a rail lines up with or without badges, and on the web the active card is announced as pressed. The published Storybook still shows the older generated page.
